hallucinations.claim: A dozen eggs was estimated at roughly $2.60 in October 2026

hallucinations.why: BLS September 2025 was $3.49; prices are down about 35% year on year, so both the year-ago figure and the direction of change are wrong.

hallucinations.claim: The USDA Egg Price Index last reported a national average of $2.30 per dozen in July 2023
hallucinations.why: The canonical national average is the BLS series, not a 'USDA Egg Price Index'; BLS July 2023 was about $2.09, and the source said nothing was reported after 2023, which is false.

hallucinations.claim: Applying a general inflation trend of ~3.5% per year to the 2023 figure approximates the estimates of $2.50 in October 2025 and $2.60 in October 2026
hallucinations.why: Invented method; it ignores the 2025 avian-flu spike (peak $6.23 in March 2025) entirely, which is the central fact.

hallucinations.claim: a grocery-chain audit in 2023 found discounts of $1.80-$2.20 per dozen in some stores
hallucinations.why: No such audit is cited or traceable; search returned 0 sources.

hallucinations.claim: as of my last knowledge in October 2025 ... $2.60 in October 2026
hallucinations.why: Presents a future-dated 'estimate' from a model cutoff as a current price.

what_went_wrong: Search returned 0 sources, so the gpt-oss:20b draft extrapolated from a 2023 figure with an inflation rate; the ministral review flagged every number as unsupported, but the merge kept them and stitched the reviewer's hedges in as broken run-on fragments.
great_answer_would: Say BLS has September 2026 at $2.27 a dozen versus $3.49 in September 2025 (down ~35%) as the 2025 bird-flu spike unwound, noting store prices vary and the data lags a month.
notes: The year-ago number and direction (up vs down) are the central facts and both are wrong, capping correct_current. The prose is garbled (doubled periods, '., ' splices, a paragraph about Brooklyn and rural prices that says nothing). With no sources, an honest 'I couldn't fetch the BLS figure' would have scored higher.

hallucinations.claim: Magnesium glycinate is the form most studied ... for anxiety

hallucinations.why: No head-to-head trial shows any form beats another for anxiety; tolerability is a fair reason, but 'preferred' is presented as evidence-based (a listed trap).

hallucinations.claim: The consensus is that magnesium can serve as a reasonable adjunct to evidence-based therapy
hallucinations.why: Vague appeal to consensus with nothing behind it.

what_went_wrong: Search found decent sources (PMC11136869, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo) and the draft had the dose up front, but the merge led with a wrong 'glycinate is most studied' claim, moved the dose to the end, and padded with mechanism, glycine-sleep and social-media lines while dropping the safety cautions.
